---
title: "Your app: explore a dataset"
subtitle: "Putting it all together, step by step"
---

We build the app that will go online on Day 2. The user:

1. chooses a dataset (or uploads their own) and loads it
2. chooses the X and Y variables **among the columns of that dataset**
3. clicks to update the plot and the summary

We build it in four steps. Each step is a working app: run it, check it, then move on. The files of each step are in [`apps/`](https://github.com/ottaviae/stat-shiny/tree/main/apps) (`05-explore-step1` … `05-explore-step4`).

```{shinylive-r}
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 330
## file: ui.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step1/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step1/server.R >}}
```

## Step 2 · Menus built from the data

The X and Y menus cannot be written in `ui.R`: their choices are the **column names**, and we know them only after the data are loaded. So:

- in `ui.R` we reserve **an empty slot** with `uiOutput()`
- in `server.R`, `renderUI()` creates the `selectInput()` and puts it in that slot

```r
# ui.R
uiOutput("x_ui")                               # <1>
```
1. An empty slot for a piece of UI that the server will create

```r
# server.R
vars <- reactive({                             # <1>
  names(dataInput())
})

output$x_ui <- renderUI({                      # <2>
  selectInput("x", "X variable:",              # <3>
              choices = vars(),
              selected = vars()[1])
})
```
1. The column names, as a reactive expression: they change when new data are loaded
2. `renderUI()` is the partner of `uiOutput()`
3. A normal `selectInput()`, with ID `x`: from now on the server can read `input$x`, like any other input

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 420
## file: ui.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step2/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step2/server.R >}}
```

Load `rock`, then `cars`: the menus change with the data. Before the first click the slots are empty, because `vars()` needs `dataInput()`, which waits for the button.

## Step 3 · The analysis, on demand

A second button, `analyze`, and a second `eventReactive()` that **freezes** the selected columns when it is clicked. The plot and the summary use only these frozen data.

```r
newdata <- eventReactive(input$analyze, {      # <1>
  df <- dataInput()
  df[, c(input$x, input$y), drop = FALSE]      # <2>
})
```
1. Runs only when *Update analysis* is clicked
2. Keep only the two chosen columns. `input$x` and `input$y` are text (the column names), so we can use them to select columns

The plot adapts to the type of X: a **boxplot** if X is categorical, a **scatterplot** if it is numeric.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 720
## file: ui.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step3/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step3/server.R >}}
```

Try it: load `cars`, choose the variables, click *Update analysis*. Now change the variables **without** clicking: the plot does not move until you click again.

## Step 4 · Upload your own data

Last step: a fourth option, *Upload data*. When it is selected, a file input and the choice of the column separator appear.

```r
conditionalPanel(                                      # <1>
  condition = "input.dataset == '4'",                  # <2>
  fileInput("file", "Select a CSV file", accept = ".csv"),
  radioButtons("sep", "Column separator",
               choices = c(";" = ";", "," = ","))
)
```
1. Shows its content only when the condition is true
2. The condition is written in **JavaScript**, not in R: `input.dataset` with a dot, and `'4'` in quotes (remember: the value of a `selectInput()` is text)

And in the server, a fourth case in `dataInput()`:

```r
} else {
  req(input$file)                                    # <1>
  read.csv(input$file$datapath, sep = input$sep)     # <2>
}
```
1. `req()` = *required*: if no file has been uploaded yet, stop here **silently**, without an error
2. Read the file from the place where Shiny saved it, with the separator chosen by the user

Test files: [example.csv](../data/example.csv) (separator `,`) and [example-semicolon.csv](../data/example-semicolon.csv) (separator `;`).

```{shinylive-r}

#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 800
## file: ui.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step4/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/05-explore-step4/server.R >}}
```

With `example.csv`, choose `condition` as X and `tr` as Y: you get a boxplot.

## Put it in your project

Copy `ui.R` and `server.R` of [`apps/05-explore-step4`](https://github.com/ottaviae/stat-shiny/tree/main/apps/05-explore-step4) into your project `my-shiny-app`, replacing the old ones, and run it with *Run App*.

**This is the app that goes online on Day 2.** Keep the project folder safe.

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 1 · Make it yours (if you have time)

Pick one or more:

1. Add `"iris" = 5` to the datasets (remember to add the case in `dataInput()`)
2. Use the **wrong separator** on purpose with `example.csv`: what happens to the menus? Why?
3. Add a `tableOutput()` that shows the first 6 rows of `newdata()`
4. Show the **title** of the plot with the names of the two variables (`main = paste(...)`)
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hints 1

1. `selectInput()`: `choices = c(..., "Upload data" = 4, "iris" = 5)`; `dataInput()`: add `else if (input$dataset == 5) { iris }` **before** the final `else`
2. With the wrong separator `read.csv()` reads a single column with a long name: the menus offer only one variable
3. `ui.R`: `tableOutput("rows")`; `server.R`: `output$rows <- renderTable({ head(newdata()) })`
4. `plot(x, y, ..., main = paste(names(df)[2], "by", names(df)[1]))`
:::
